visuals.title: What the failing liver stops doing

glossary.Nodular regeneration: Liver cells regrowing in disorganised lumps between bands of scar tissue.
glossary.Liver architecture: The normal organised arrangement of liver cells, vessels and bile ducts.
glossary.Liver failure: Loss of the liver's ability to make proteins, clear toxins and process bilirubin.
glossary.Macrocytic anaemia: Anaemia with abnormally large red cells, common in heavy alcohol use.
glossary.AST:ALT ratio: Ratio of two liver enzymes; above 2 suggests alcohol-related liver disease.
glossary.GGT: Gamma-glutamyl transferase, a liver enzyme raised by alcohol and bile duct disease.
glossary.Chronic viral hepatitis: Long-term liver infection with hepatitis B or C virus.
glossary.Hepatitis C: A blood-borne virus that causes chronic hepatitis and cirrhosis.
glossary.Spirometry: A breathing test measuring how much and how fast air can be blown out.
glossary.Sarcoidosis: A multisystem disease with non-caseating granulomas, often in lungs and lymph nodes.
glossary.Erythema nodosum: Tender red nodules on the shins caused by inflammation of fat under the skin.
glossary.Jaundice: Yellowing of skin and eyes from raised bilirubin.
glossary.Encephalopathy: Brain dysfunction causing confusion, drowsiness or coma.
glossary.Peripheral oedema: Swelling of the legs and ankles from fluid in the tissues.
glossary.Hypoglycaemia: Low blood glucose; the cirrhotic liver stores and releases glucose poorly.
glossary.Palmar nodule: A small firm lump in the palm, the first stage of Dupuytren's contracture.
glossary.E. coli: Escherichia coli, a gut bacterium and the commonest cause of SBP.
glossary.Klebsiella pneumoniae: A Gram-negative gut bacterium that can cause SBP and pneumonia.
glossary.Hypercoagulability: An increased tendency of the blood to clot.
glossary.Endoscopy: A camera passed into the gut, here to look for and band oesophageal varices.
glossary.Endoscopic ultrasound: Ultrasound performed from a probe on an endoscope inside the gut.
glossary.Oesophageal varices: Dilated veins in the lower oesophagus caused by portal hypertension, which can bleed heavily.
glossary.Synthetic function: The liver's ability to make proteins such as albumin and clotting factors.
glossary.Prothrombin time: A clotting test; prolonged when the liver makes too few clotting factors.
glossary.Albumin: The main blood protein, made by the liver; low levels mean poor synthetic function.
glossary.Ishak staging: A biopsy score of how much fibrosis is present in the liver.
glossary.Germ-cell cancer: Cancer of the cells that make sperm or eggs, such as testicular teratoma.
glossary.Antiviral therapy: Drugs that suppress or clear a virus, such as hepatitis B or C.
glossary.Primary prevention: Treatment to stop a complication happening for the first time.
glossary.Variceal bleeding: Bleeding from ruptured varices, usually presenting as haematemesis.
glossary.Ammonia: A toxic product of protein breakdown, normally cleared by the liver.
glossary.NH4+: Ammonium, the charged form of ammonia, which cannot cross the gut wall.
glossary.Colonic pH: The acidity of the contents of the large bowel.
glossary.Ciprofloxacin: A quinolone antibiotic used to prevent recurrent SBP.
glossary.Norfloxacin: A quinolone antibiotic used as SBP prophylaxis.
glossary.Broad-spectrum antibiotics: Antibiotics active against a wide range of bacteria.
glossary.APTT: Activated partial thromboplastin time, a clotting test of the intrinsic pathway.
glossary.LVP: Large-volume paracentesis: draining several litres of ascites through a needle.
glossary.Collagen: The main structural protein of scar tissue.
glossary.Fibrotic septa: Bands of scar tissue that divide the liver into nodules.
glossary.Intrahepatic vascular resistance: Resistance to blood flow through the liver, raised by scarring.
glossary.Splanchnic capillary pressure: Pressure in the small vessels of the gut, raised by portal hypertension.
glossary.Coagulopathy: Impaired blood clotting causing a bleeding tendency.
glossary.Clotting factors: Proteins made by the liver that make blood clot.
glossary.Sequestration: Trapping of blood cells in an enlarged spleen.
glossary.Splenic congestion: Engorgement of the spleen with blood because of raised portal pressure.
glossary.Detoxification: The liver's removal of toxins such as ammonia and drugs from the blood.
glossary.Hepatocellular carcinoma: Primary liver cancer, which cirrhosis greatly increases the risk of.
